name: Lemon Tree Hotels Ltd
title: Lemon Tree Hotels Ltd - 541233 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q2 FY27 hotel RevPAR up 18% to Rs 5,137 on occupancy gain of 633 bps; net EBITDA margin 44.6%, but prior FY28 margin and 2,000-key opening guidance remain unproven as 1H net adds were only about 550 keys.

triggers.quote: occupancy was at 76.1%, up 633 basis points YoY

triggers.label: Gross ARR Rs 6,751, up 8%
triggers.quote: our Gross ARR stood at Rs. 6,751, up 8% YoY

triggers.label: Gross openings ~2,000 keys reaffirmed
triggers.quote: from a gross opening of 2,000, which is what I had mentioned last time, we are absolutely on track

summary.headline: Lemon Tree Q2 FY27 best-ever Q2: revenue Rs 363.8 crore (+18% YoY), net EBITDA margin 44.6%, PAT up 90% to Rs 79.8 crore.
summary.overview: Lemon Tree posted its best-ever second quarter, with Gross ARR up 8% YoY to Rs 6,751, occupancy up 633 bps to 76.1% and RevPAR up 18% to Rs 5,137. Net EBITDA rose 22% to Rs 162.2 crore, with margin at 44.6% (47.7% excluding a 3.2% of revenue hit from SAR provision and GST). Reported PAT was lifted by a net Rs 22 crore non-cash exceptional item linked to the Gurgaon lease termination. Management reiterated the 55/45 H2/H1 revenue split and a Fleur Hotels demerger listing in CY27, while guiding to about 2,000 gross keys opening in FY27.

financial_highlights.change: +157 bps YoY; 47.7% like-to-like excluding SAR and GST impact of 3.2% of revenue
+90% YoY; includes net exceptional gain of about Rs 22 crore
down 11% from Rs 1,610.2 crore a year ago

segments.name: Fleur Hotels (owned portfolio)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 337 crore (+15% YoY), hotel EBITDAR margin 53% (+112 bps). Keys RevPAR Rs 3,109 (+29%), occupancy 69.7% (+976 bps), ARR Rs 4,460 (+11%), Keys EBITDAR margin 50% (+748 bps).

segments.name: Asset-light (managed and franchised)
segments.commentary: Opened 8 hotels with 523 rooms and signed 11 hotels with 825 rooms in Q2. Pipeline and operating inventory is 24,061 rooms across 285 hotels; 130 hotels with 12,131 rooms are operational.

segments.name: Food and beverage
segments.commentary: F&B growth was similar to RevPAR growth, driven by MICE and banqueting; management called it nothing extraordinary.

guidance_outlook: Revenue split guided at 55% H2 / 45% H1 and EBITDA at 60/40; management said the Q3 read depends on post-Diwali demand.
Gross opening of about 2,000 keys in FY27, with 900+ keys guided for H2; management said there is no line of sight to material further deflagging.
Renovation spend to fall to about 1.2% of revenue next year from current elevated levels; management expects this to add about 1.5% to Fleur margins.
Fleur to list in CY27; about 2,500 rooms targeted operational within 9-12 months of listing, with FY30-FY31 as the broader timeline.
Management guides about Rs 3,000 crore total capex over the next 3.5 years, contingent on acquisitions and new properties.
capex_capacity: Bandra East (Lemon Tree Premier Bandra): land bought for about Rs 120 crore; about 172 rooms, expected to open in FY30; ARR underwritten at about Rs 12,000 at opening; management targets 12-13% ROCE.
Aurika Shimla: 90 owned rooms, scheduled to open in Q3 FY27.
Aurika Shillong: 165 leased rooms, expected to open in FY28.
Aurika Varanasi: 47 leased heritage rooms, piling started, opening expected in FY29.

Aurika Nehru Place: DDA letter of award extended to August 2027; now about 610 rooms (from about 570); opening expected CY31, pending Ridge Management Board and tree-felling approvals (about 350 trees, 3,500 to be replanted).
Renovation spend in FY27 so far: about Rs 200 crore including the Bombay buyout (about Rs 130 crore). Renovation split is about 60-65% opex, balance capex.
Warburg Pincus investment of Rs 960 crore is on call, to be drawn only when deployed; management is nearly 100% sure the full amount will be taken.
demand_pricing: Corporate demand remains muted due to oil prices, inflation and current-account concerns; IT new-hire demand in Gurgaon has not picked up. Non-negotiated (retail and FIT) business has grown.
Revenue above Rs 7,500 ARR rose to 50% of revenue from 48% last year; GST at 18% applies above Rs 7,500 per night.
Aurika ARR grew about 9%, the highest in many quarters; management intends to lean more on ARR for Aurika as occupancy has stabilised around 75%.
Management says supply growth is concentrated in Tier 2-4 markets rather than deep-demand cities and does not see supply outpacing demand.
Loyalty members are about 25% of business and repeat guests about 45%; loyalty payout is about 4% of revenue with 30-40% breakage.

qa_highlights.question: How should the 2H outlook and FIT revival be viewed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management kept the 55/45 H2/H1 revenue split and said corporate demand is still muted; non-negotiated business has offset it. The Q3 outlook will be clearer after Diwali and wedding season, likely discussed after Q3 results.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Gurgaon lease terminated and what drove the exceptional item?
qa_highlights.answer: A fire-related withdrawal of the basement banquet approval (about 30% of that hotel's business) led to termination in August. The net Rs 22 crore positive exceptional item is a Rs 41 crore lease reversal, less about Rs 16 crore property tax provision and Rs 3 crore associate write-down; non-cash.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Bandra East investment justified given BKC pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites Mumbai EBITDA of Rs 22-25 lakh per key against about Rs 2 crore investment per key, and targets 12-13% ROCE at about Rs 12,000 ARR, based on a small Kalina hotel earning Rs 7,500-8,000 ARR at 80% occupancy.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Bombay/Bandra FY30 timeline hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Design is complete; excavation to start in 2-3 weeks, with approvals and superstructure in 3-5 months and a 33-month build. Management said the timeline could slip.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Fleur management fees lagging revenue, and why?
qa_highlights.answer: Management fees are about one-third to 40% GOP-linked; the 2-3% margin drag from renovations and GST reduced fees. Renovation drops to 1.2% of revenue next year, adding about 1.5% to margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Omaxe MoU and its timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Asset-light: about 4,000 rooms across 10 properties, 9 greenfield, mostly township and bus-station PPP sites; Lemon Tree is manager and brand owner with no capex. One Greater Noida property may open in 12-18 months, others in 3-3.5 years.

risks_watch: Corporate demand recovery depends on oil, inflation and the war; management said the corporate side is still muted.
Deflagging: about 530 rooms removed, including 450 ex-Gurgaon; the 2,500-key FY28 guidance was stated as net of deflagging risk.
Aurika Nehru Place and Bandra East timelines depend on DDA and Ridge Management Board approvals and a dense Mumbai build.
Maldives acquisition is on hold after the government's 40% local-currency revenue rule.
Exceptional items (property tax, GST demands) are recurring in nature; management said they are not predictable.
Pro forma asset-light EBITDA margin is about 56%, below the 70%+ target; management cites operating leverage over 3-4 years.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operating performance and the Q2 numbers, but noticeably cautious on H2 and corporate demand, and evasive on specifics beyond the next quarter. Management was also candid that the Nehru Place and Bandra timelines depend on external approvals.
key_quotes: Q2 FY27 was our best-ever second quarter, with the highest Q2 ARR, revenue, EBITDA, PBT, PAT and cash profit.
There is nothing on the paper for deflagging in Q3 and Q4.
Our investment, which will fructify three years later, will be at roughly Rs. 2 crore a key.
Our learning is that at all times, we must be cost warriors.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Renovation spend falls to about 1.2% of revenue next year, adding about 1.5% to Fleur margins, while Q2 net EBITDA margin was 44.6% (47.7% like-to-like); asset-light margin is ~56% vs a 70%+ target over 3-4 years.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q3 FY27 onward; ~2,000 keys FY27, 900+ in H2
rows.why: About 2,000 gross keys guided to open in FY27 with 900+ in H2; Aurika Shimla (90 owned rooms) is scheduled for Q3 FY27, and 8 asset-light hotels (523 rooms) opened in Q2.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Occupancy rose 633 bps to 76.1% and RevPAR grew 18% to Rs 5,137 in Q2, with the 2,000-key opening programme and 24,061-room asset-light pipeline supporting volume.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Rs 3,000 crore capex guided over 3.5 years, Bandra East land (~Rs 120 crore) already bought, and Rs 960 crore Warburg Pincus money on call; occupancy is only ~76%, so new capex is planned but mostly contingent on acquisitions and approvals.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numeric FY27 revenue or margin upgrade was given; management stayed cautious on H2 and corporate demand, with Q2 Gross ARR up only 8% and occupancy at 76.1%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management kept the 55/45 H2/H1 revenue split but called corporate demand muted and said the Q3 read depends on post-Diwali demand; exceptional items and Nehru Place/Bandra approvals are also risks.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Aurika Shimla (90 rooms) opens Q3 FY27 and Aurika Shillong (165 leased rooms) is expected in FY28, with Aurika ARR up about 9%.

rows.label: Gross debt down 11% YoY to Rs 1,429.2 crore
rows.why: Gross debt fell from Rs 1,610.2 crore to Rs 1,429.2 crore and cost of debt dropped 28 bps to 7.44%, lowering interest drag.

rows.label: Fleur Hotels demerger listing in CY27
rows.why: Management reiterated the Fleur demerger listing in CY27, with about 2,500 rooms targeted operational within 9-12 months of listing.

rows.label: Asset-light pipeline of 24,061 rooms across 285 hotels
rows.why: Q2 saw 11 hotels (825 rooms) signed and 8 opened (523 rooms), with 130 hotels (12,131 rooms) already operational, supporting management fee growth of 19% to Rs 40.8 crore.

tone.note: Management was confident on Q2 operating numbers and the FY27 opening pipeline but cautious on H2 and corporate demand, and candid that Nehru Place and Bandra timelines depend on external approvals; analysts probed the Bandra East ROCE case, the Gurgaon exceptional item and the Fleur management fee

oneOffs.what: Net ~Rs 22 cr non-cash exceptional gain from Gurgaon lease termination (Rs 41 cr lease reversal less ~Rs 16 cr property tax provision and Rs 3 cr associate write-down) inflates PAT growth of +90%; doe
3.2% of revenue hit from SAR provision and GST in Q2 FY27 depresses reported net EBITDA margin (44.6% reported vs 47.7% like-to-like)

quality.why: Revenue +18% is driven by occupancy (+633 bps to 76.1%) with ARR only +8%, so volume/occupancy is the main driver and growth is organic from the existing hotel base; the 90% PAT jump is flattered by a net ~Rs 22 cr non-cash exceptional gain, which would not recur, while the SAR/GST provision is a minor drag on margin.
